title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: k is a field of characteristic p>0, G is a p-divisible (Barsotti–Tate) group over k, and G* is its Cartier/Serre dual. Write g = dim G and g* = dim G*. The page continues the previous one ('Dualité des modules de Dieudonné de groupes de B.T. duals l'un de l'autre … le module de Dieudonné réduit M⊗_W k'). Its goal is to describe the reduced Dieudonné module mod p intrinsically, through Lie algebras of universal vector extensions.

(i) Universal extension. The 'groupe enveloppant' G̃ = E(G) sits in 0 → 𝕍(t_{G*}) → G̃ → G → 0. Here 𝕍(E) = Spec Sym(E) in EGA notation, so the vector group has Lie algebra t_{G*}^∨ = ω_{G*}. Taking Lie algebras gives 0 → ω_{G*} → t_{G̃} → t_G → 0, of ranks g*, g+g*, g. This is the Mazur–Messing exact sequence for Lie E(G).

(ii) Reduced Dieudonné module. Grothendieck sets H(G) = t_{G̃*} (the 'NB'). It carries the Hodge filtration 0 → ω_G = t_G^∨ → H(G) → t_{G*} → 0, of ranks g, g+g*, g*. Functoriality applied to Frobenius and Verschiebung gives F_0 = H(F): H(G)^{(p)} → H(G) and V_0 = H(V): H(G) → H(G)^{(p)}. These are compatible with the filtrations; the Frobenius twists ω_G^{(p)}, t_{G*}^{(p)} appear in the lower row.

(1) The sequences for t_{G̃} and t_{G̃*} are transposes of each other under a canonical functorial pairing Lie E(G) × Lie E(G*) → k, and this pairing exchanges F_0 and V_0. In modern terms this is the perfect pairing D(G)×D(G*) → D(μ_{p^∞}) reduced mod p, i.e. Dieudonné module duality.

(2) Ker F_0 = Im V_0 = ω_G^{(p)} and Ker V_0 = Im F_0. The first is the mod-p statement 'VM/pM ↔ Hodge filtration'. The second is said to be provable by a (partly illegible) argument. Together they make (H(G), F_0, V_0) the Dieudonné module of G reduced mod p, i.e. the Dieudonné module of G[p].

(3)–(4) Since Ker F_0 = ω_G^{(p)}, F_0 factors through t_{G*}^{(p)}. The composite t_{G*}^{(p)} → H(G) → t_{G*} is identified with Frobenius on H^1(G, O_G), i.e. the Hasse–Witt map. Then:
- G is purely infinitesimal (connected) ⇔ F_0 is nilpotent on H(G), equivalently the Hasse–Witt map is nilpotent.
- Dually, G* is infinitesimal (G has no 'toroidal'/multiplicative part) ⇔ V_0 is nilpotent.
- G and G* are both infinitesimal (local–local) ⇔ F_0 and V_0 are both nilpotent.

The page is building the dictionary between the crystalline/universal-extension description of Dieudonné modules and the classical one, as preparation for the 1970 Nice and Montreal lectures.
errors: The marginal '?' next to (4) signals that Grothendieck was unsure of the identification of the composite with Frobenius on H^1(G,O_G). The identification is correct (it is the Hasse–Witt map). The equivalence 'F_0 nilpotent ⇔ Hasse–Witt nilpotent' also holds, because F_0 factors through t_{G*}^{(p)}.

Under the Corollaire, 'G purement infinitésimal i.e. G* sans tore' and 'G sans composante toroïdale' should be read as 'no multiplicative part' for p-divisible groups. 'Tore' is loose terminology here, not an error of substance.
In (2), 'Ker V_0 = Im F_0' is asserted with only a sketched or illegible justification. It is true (exactness of Dieudonné modules of G[p]), so this is a gap on the page rather than an error.
The bottom-left label of the lower row reads ω_{G}^{(p)}; it correctly matches t_G^{∨(p)}. No mathematical error otherwise.

deep.surprise_reason: These are working notes reconstructing standard facts: universal extension, Hodge filtration, F/V duality, Ker F = Im V, and the Hasse–Witt nilpotence criteria. All were subsequently published by Grothendieck (Nice/Montréal), Messing, Mazur–Messing and BBM, or are classical. The only historical interest is seeing the definition H(G) = Lie E(G*) being worked out in Pisa around 1969, contemporaneous with Oda.
transcription_corrections: Header: 'dual des' (not 'dual de') above the right-hand diagram.
NB line: H(G) = t_{G̃*}, with a tilde over G* (partly scribbled out on the page).
(1) reads roughly 'suites exactes pour t_{G̃} et t_{G̃*} transposées l'une de l'autre par un accouplement canonique fonctoriel, pour lequel F_0 et V_0 s'interchangent (ceci vaut en car p)'.

(4) bracket reads '[il correspond : Frobenius dans H^1(G, O_G)]'. The following line is 'G purement infinitésimal ⟺ F_0 nilpotent dans H(G) = t_{G̃*}'; the struck-out 'La composée …' line contains t_{G*}^{(p)} →^{F_0} H(G) → t_{G*}.
Corollaire: 'G purement infinitésimal i.e. G* sans tore' and 'G* purement infinitésimal i.e. G sans composante toroïdale ⟺ V_0 nilpotent'.
